clue.text: Tried to get unauthorised information about Conservative with mace?

indicators.note: the spying word goes about, or around, the party letter, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to spy is to try to get information you are not entitled to; past tense spied

explanation.surface: Someone snooping on a Tory politician who is armed with a spray of mace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with mace' looks like a weapon spray, but mace is also the spice made from nutmeg husks, so the definition means seasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice, so food prepared with it has been seasoned with spice.

clue.text: Intending to ignore Liberal's criticism

indicators.note: ignoring the party letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: planning means intending to do something
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Planning to disregard a Liberal's critical comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Panning is harsh criticism, as when a reviewer slates a show.

clue.text: Focus, say, on diamonds, or one of them?

parts.note: the Ford Focus is an example of a car
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Concentrate on a suit of gems, or on a single gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus' is the Ford model, not concentration; 'one of them' points back to the diamonds as a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is a suit in a pack, and each one is a playing card.

clue.text: Ocean boy engaging one with description of profound scheming

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the ocean

indicators.note: the boy engages, or holds within him, the number one

parts.note: a lad is a boy
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A sea-going lad caught up in a description of devious plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-laid plot is one carefully and secretly prepared well in advance.

clue.text: One in distress typically blocks American railway

parts.note: dams are barriers that block water
EL is the American elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A heroine in trouble obstructs a US train line, like a film stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase 'damsel in distress'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock figure of romance rescued by a hero is the young maiden in distress.

clue.text: Detective's ethical standards apt to convey a message?

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels
a code is a set of moral rules

explanation.surface: An Oxford sleuth's moral principles are likely to send a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the detective of a popular British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot-and-dash system is used to transmit messages by telegraph or light.

clue.text: Clever European impolite about IT

indicators.note: the rude word goes about, or around, the two letters

parts.note: rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A smart European is rude about information technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means learned, showing great knowledge.

clue.text: Study Greek tune being played — it's suitable

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: a tune being played suggests its notes being worked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Learning a Greek melody that is being performed seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being played' rearranges TUNE to UENT, after CON and GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent means in agreement or harmony, hence fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Throwing us, practised part of slapstick routine?

indicators.note: throwing suggests flinging letters about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hurling things at us is a well-rehearsed piece of comic business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing' fits the surface, as these are thrown in slapstick, but rearranges US PRACTISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling cream-filled pastries into faces is a classic piece of knockabout comedy.

clue.text: Area of golf course in summer ought to be cut

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them
the outer letters of the phrase are cut away, leaving only the run in the middle

explanation.surface: A patch of the golf course that needs mowing this summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rough is the long grass bordering the fairway of a golf course.

clue.text: Having good storage capacity, like tower block accommodation?

explanation.definitionFit: Disks that pack data tightly have large capacity; tower blocks pack many residents onto a small plot of ground.

clue.text: Hit Timothy's back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the possessive name from right to left

parts.note: Tim's: Tim is short for Timothy

explanation.surface: Someone struck Timothy on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part but turns TIMS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Smit is an archaic past tense of smite, to strike.

clue.text: Engine almost lacks potential for easing off

indicators.note: potential means what could be made, so the letters may become something else
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A motor without enough power is slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ENGINE to ENGIN; 'potential' rearranges ENGIN and LACKS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Slackening is loosening or reducing in intensity, a synonym of easing off.

clue.text: Short month's food allowance-nothing to go with cheese

indicators.note: short means the month name is cut down to its familiar abbreviated form

parts.note: August, one of the months

indicators.note: to go means the following letter is removed from the allowance word

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A month's meagre food ration, with nothing to accompany the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts AUGUST to AUG; 'nothing to go' removes O from RATION, leaving RATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish cooked au gratin has a browned topping, usually of grated cheese and breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Terrible actor ruined with debts

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the word's letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A performer brought to ruin by what he owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means extremely bad or appalling.

clue.text: Donne works standing up?

indicators.note: works suggests the poet's name being worked into a new form, an anagram

explanation.surface: The poems of John Donne hold up well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like the poet's writings, but rearranges DONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on end is upright, vertical rather than lying down.

clue.text: Sect by Russian river concerned with civilisation

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
the Ural river flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A religious group beside a Russian river cares about civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultural relates to the arts, customs and ideas of a society.

clue.text: Put off person on special regime one abandoned

indicators.note: the one is abandoned, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a dieter follows a special eating regime
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A slimmer gives up on their diet plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage, to put someone off doing something.

clue.text: Devil shows anger-about time

indicators.note: the anger word is placed about the time letter, surrounding it

parts.note: temper means anger, as in losing one's temper

explanation.surface: The devil displays rage about time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is the great tempter, who lures people into sin.

clue.text: Ancient Babylonian suffering aneurism

indicators.note: suffering implies being in a disturbed state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An old inhabitant of Mesopotamia has an aneurism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumer was the ancient civilisation of southern Mesopotamia, later part of Babylonia.

clue.text: Characters with a leaning to the right?

definitions.text: Characters with a leaning to the right?

parts.words: Characters with a leaning to the right?
parts.note: sounds like people with right-wing politics, but means printed letters that slope rightwards

explanation.surface: People with conservative political sympathies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type, used for emphasis, is a style whose letters slant to the right.

clue.text: Lay off about prohibition in state capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the ban, enclosing it
off means not right, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Sacking workers over a ban in a US state's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LAY to ALY, then 'about' puts BAN inside. Albany is the capital of New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Albany is the seat of government of New York State.

clue.text: Perfect team claim wrongly to accommodate university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another letter, accommodating it inside
wrongly says the words are put in the wrong order, an anagram

explanation.surface: A side makes a false claim of being flawless to house a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges TEAM CLAIM; 'to accommodate' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate means spotless or without flaw.

clue.text: French performer in station

indicators.note: the performer's name is found within the next word

explanation.surface: A French entertainer at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was a French comic actor and film-maker, hiding in 'sTATIon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a French comedian and film director, famous for Monsieur Hulot.

clue.text: King of Mercia, bad one

parts.note: off means gone bad, as food does
a means one

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king was a bad one.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia and built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was the eighth-century ruler of Mercia in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Some tennis to begin

parts.note: a set is one portion of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Time for a bit of tennis to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden word signal, but 'Some tennis' is a set.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is to start work on something in earnest.

clue.text: Insubstantial result of astronomer meeting fellow astronomer

parts.note: George Airy was a nineteenth-century Astronomer Royal
Airy again, the same Astronomer Royal

explanation.surface: What happens when one stargazer meets another is flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir George Airy was a British Astronomer Royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy means vague, fanciful and lacking substance.

clue.text: Poet carrying vessel of a greenish colour

indicators.note: the poet's name carries the ship inside it, enclosing it

parts.note: Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A poet aboard a vessel turning slightly green.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray was an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassy describes a colour like that of lawn or meadow, a fresh green.

clue.text: Contact in Anatolia is excellent

indicators.note: the word lies inside the words that follow, across their joins

explanation.surface: Getting in touch in Turkey is very good.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to communicate and cooperate with someone, to get in touch.
